video_title: Lou Williams On Entering The NBA Draft Unprepared & Adjusting To Life As A Rookie

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on realizing he could be a pro prospect
quotes.excerpt: that was the first time I thought to myself, oh shit, I can do this.
quotes.quote: We were at USA in Colorado training for Junior Olympics or World Games. I, Monta, CJ, Blatche, Martell Webster, Gerald Green were all the same class. We were watching the draft together and I remember it, at 13, Sebastian Telfair went. That was the first time I thought to myself, oh shit, I can do this. At that time, it was guys like you, Mac, that were already physically there. You are 6'7, 6'8, 6'9, y'all are built like men. That was the first time I saw a guy my size have that opportunity and I'm like, man, if the door is open for guys at this size and I think I am who I am, I'm out of here. I'm going.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on the lack of information before the draft
quotes.excerpt: Ain't nobody tell me nothing. I was very clear, T-Mac. Ain't nobody tell me nothing.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: What information did you get from outside?

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Ain't nobody tell me nothing. I was very clear, T-Mac. Ain't nobody tell me nothing.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on being drafted 45th due to lack of preparation
quotes.excerpt: I got picked 45 because I wasn't in shape, I wasn't ready, I didn't take the workouts serious.
quotes.quote: That's why I got picked 45 because I wasn't in shape, I wasn't ready, I didn't take the workouts serious. I just was going on being naive to think, hey look, if these guys can do it and I'm in the conversation of guys going, I want to be one of them too. I don't care where I get drafted, I'm going to the league. I don't want to do with school.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on treating his rookie season like an internship
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to look at this like a job and this is a career.
quotes.quote: The work that it takes, the discipline that it takes, some of the sacrifices, knowing that you can go play at the next level but this is a necessary step I got to take to get there, I didn't have none of that in my system. So I figured, look, I'm going to look at this like a job and this is a career. If I get drafted anywhere, if I get a foot in the door, it becomes an internship to me now.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on the challenge of finding a role as a rookie
quotes.excerpt: The most challenging thing for me my rookie year was just to be able to find a role.
quotes.quote: The most challenging thing for me my rookie year was just to be able to find a role, be able to find my place in being an 18-year-old kid, not knowing you're going to play, but knowing you're expected to show up, knowing you're expected to do all of the extra things. How do you stay motivated and how do I stick if I'm not going to play being so young?

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on Mo Cheeks' advice during his rookie season
quotes.excerpt: You better get that ball to Kyle Korver, you better get that ball to Willie Green.
quotes.quote: Mo Cheeks was like, hey man, in practice, you better get that ball to Kyle Korver, you better get that ball to Willie Green and John Salmons and you better make sure them guys get shots. You stay out the way, young fella. He was training me to be another version of Mo Cheeks.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on Mo Cheeks admitting he coached him wrong
quotes.excerpt: He said, man, I've been coaching you the wrong way this whole time.
quotes.quote: Mo had called me to the back of the plane and I sit down with him and he's sitting there watching my high school highlights. He said, man, I've been coaching you the wrong way this whole time. From now on out, you go out there and you be yourself. Play your game.
